page.h1: HTS Chapter 21: Miscellaneous Edible Preparations — U.S. Exports & Foreign Tariffs

seo.title: U.S. Food Preparation & Supplement Exports by Country (HTS Ch. 21) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: The U.S. exported $11.72B of food preparations in 2025: $7.54B of supplements, protein powders and mixes, $2.37B of sauces. Top buyers and what each charges.

intro:
The U.S. exported **$11.72 billion** of Chapter 21 food preparations in 2025, up **3.6%** from 2024. Heading 2106, which holds dietary supplements, protein powders and concentrates, drink mixes, flavored syrups and creamers, was **$7.54 billion**, 64% of the chapter. Sauces, dressings and seasonings followed at $2.37 billion (including $390 million of ketchup), then soups and broths ($945 million), coffee and tea extracts ($444 million), ice cream ($255 million) and yeasts ($161 million). Canada (**28%**) and Mexico (**18%**) buy almost half, followed by South Korea (5%) and China (4%). Exports from January to August 2026 were 5.7% above the same months of 2025.

For most of this trade the tariff is zero: Canada and Mexico under USMCA, South Korea under KORUS, Australia under AUSFTA, and Hong Kong charges no tariffs at all. Since July 1, 2026 the EU lets 250,000 tonnes a year of U.S. Chapter 21 goods in at about a quarter of its normal duty (3.2% instead of 12.8% on most food preparations). China is the costly market: its normal rate, its 2018–19 counter-tariffs and an extra 10% on all U.S. goods add up to about **32%** on food preparations and **47%** on sauces and soups. What usually decides access is the buyer’s food regulator: plant registration with China’s customs (GACC) and Korea’s MFDS, China’s health-food rules for supplements, and supplement-ingredient rules in Canada, the EU and Japan.

keyTakeaways: Supplements, protein powders, drink mixes and other food preparations (heading 2106) are almost two-thirds of U.S. Chapter 21 exports: $7.54 billion of $11.72 billion in 2025.

Canada put 25% on U.S. soy sauce, ketchup, mustard, mayonnaise, soups and some sugar- and dairy-based preparations from March 4 to August 31, 2025; since then it charges nothing on qualifying U.S. goods, and its September 2026 counter-tariffs skip Chapter 21.

China charges U.S. food preparations about 32% (12% normal rate + 10% counter-tariff + 10% extra), or 22% with an exclusion; exclusions end December 31, 2026 and the extra tariff could rise to 34% on January 10, 2027.
The EU’s 25–30% counter-list on almost every Chapter 21 good is suspended and never applied; instead, a 250,000-tonne U.S. quota has cut its duty to about a quarter since July 1, 2026.
